analyst.summary: South Indian Bank is showing real, not just cosmetic, improvement in loan-book quality - gross bad loans fell from over 3% to under 1.4% in a single quarter, and profit and margins are both moving in the right direction. Capital levels are comfortable and the valuation (under 8x earnings) remains inexpensive relative to the improving trend. We'd want to see this asset-quality gain sustained over a few more quarters before getting more constructive, but there's nothing here that argues for caution beyond the normal risks of a mid-sized private bank.
